title: Images and Multimedia
subtitle: Make your app visual, accessible and professional
description: Learn how to add responsive images correctly, understand alt text for accessibility and SEO, use figure and figcaption, and embed audio and video like production apps do.

blocks.text: Your app is text-only - let's make it visual

Welcome back! Right now your app from Lesson 3 is just text and links. Real apps are visual. Think of YouTube without thumbnails, or Jumia without product images - nobody would use them. Today we make your portfolio look like a real product with images, audio and video.
Open your lab: Home > Menu > Practical. You will be adding images to your index.html, about.html and projects.html today.
The img tag is not just src - it's a system

Everyone writes but production apps need more. src is where the file is, alt is mandatory description for when image fails and for blind users, width and height prevent layout shift (CLS - Cumulative Layout Shift, a Google ranking factor), loading="lazy" makes page load faster by loading images only when needed.

Most important: Never leave alt empty for important images. If image is decorative only, then alt="" is correct to tell screen readers to ignore it. But if image conveys information like your profile photo, alt must describe it meaningfully.

blocks.text: Responsive images - why your image looks blurry on phones

A 4000px image on mobile is wasteful - slow loading, data cost. Real apps serve different sizes. Use srcset to give browser options: small image for phones, large for desktops. Browser chooses best. Also sizes tells browser how much space image will take.

blocks.text: Audio and Video - not just YouTube embeds

HTML5 has native <audio> and <video> tags - no Flash needed. They support controls attribute to show play/pause, autoplay (avoid unless muted), loop, muted, poster for video thumbnail, and multiple source formats because not all browsers support same format. Always include fallback text.
Critical: autoplay with sound is blocked by most browsers to avoid annoying users. If you need autoplay, must be muted. Also preload="none" saves data - don't load video until user clicks play.

blocks.text: Accessibility - what senior devs check first

Alt text is not optional - it's law in many countries for public sites. Good alt describes content and function: alt="Prince Egyir smiling at laptop" is good, alt="image" or alt="photo" is useless. For decorative images like lines or background patterns, alt="" tells screen reader to skip it. Also never put important text inside image only - screen readers can't read text inside jpg.

blocks.question: You add without alt. It looks fine visually. Why will accessibility audit and Google Lighthouse fail it and what is correct?
options: It will pass because width/height are enough, alt is optional for local images and only required for external images

It fails because alt is mandatory for all informative images - screen readers need description, and missing width/height causes layout shift (CLS). Correct is alt with meaningful description plus width/height plus loading=lazy
It fails because jpg format requires alt but png doesn't, so convert to png to avoid alt requirement
It fails because src must be absolute URL, relative src like profile.jpg is invalid and requires alt as fallback
blocks.correctFeedback: Perfect! You understand CLS, accessibility, and why alt is mandatory - this is production-level thinking.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Think: What does screen reader announce when alt missing? What does Google measure for CLS? Is alt optional?
blocks.reasoning: Missing alt fails WCAG accessibility. Missing width/height causes layout shift (CLS) hurting SEO and UX. Both are required for production.

blocks.question: You need to show a project screenshot with caption 'My e-commerce app built for Accra market'. Which markup is semantically correct and best for SEO?
options:
My e-commerce app built for Accra market

because p is enough for captions and figure is deprecated
because figure groups image with caption semantically and figcaption is programmatically associated

My e-commerce app built for Accra market
because div and span are more flexible than figure
because title attribute replaces need for figcaption
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly! Figure/figcaption association is what Google uses to understand image context.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Which element programmatically associates caption with image for SEO and assistive tech?
blocks.reasoning: figure + figcaption semantically links image and caption. div/p doesn't. alt describes image content, figcaption provides caption/context.

blocks.question: You have a 4000px banner image. On mobile it loads slow and costs user data. You add srcset with 400w, 800w, 1200w versions and sizes="(max-width: 600px) 400px, 800px". How does browser choose?
options: Browser always loads largest image from srcset regardless of sizes to ensure best quality on all devices

Browser uses sizes to know rendered width, then picks best file from srcset based on screen width, pixel density and network - e.g., 400w for phone <600px, 800w for desktop, saving data and improving performance
srcset is ignored if src exists, browser only loads src file, srcset is just for SEO description
Browser loads all images in srcset at once to cache them for future use, so it doesn't save data
blocks.correctFeedback: Brilliant performance knowledge! This is how real apps save data and load fast on Ghana mobile networks.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: What is purpose of srcset and sizes? Do browsers load all or choose best?
blocks.reasoning: srcset provides options, sizes hints at rendered size, browser chooses optimal file based on viewport, DPR, network - key for responsive performance.

blocks.question: You have decorative divider line image that adds no information, just visual separation. What is correct alt handling and why?
options: alt="decorative divider line" because every image must have descriptive alt regardless of purpose
alt="" (empty alt) because decorative images should be ignored by screen readers to avoid noise, and empty alt tells assistive tech to skip it
Omit alt attribute completely because decorative images don't need alt attribute at all
alt="divider" and aria-hidden="false" to ensure screen readers announce decorative images
blocks.correctFeedback: Perfect accessibility knowledge! Empty alt is intentional and correct for decorative images.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Should screen readers announce every decorative line? What does empty alt signal?
blocks.reasoning: Empty alt alt="" indicates decorative image, assistive tech skips it. Omitting alt causes screen readers to announce file name, which is noisy.

blocks.question: You add <video autoplay> with sound on homepage. Chrome blocks autoplay. Users complain video doesn't play. What is correct production fix and why does Chrome block?
options: Chrome blocks autoplay with sound to prevent annoying users and save data; fix with autoplay muted or remove autoplay and let user click controls, optionally add playsinline for mobile
Chrome blocks because mp4 format is not supported, fix by converting to avi format which allows autoplay
Chrome blocks because video tag requires JavaScript to autoplay, fix by adding JavaScript autoplay script
Chrome blocks because width attribute is missing, fix by adding width="100%" to allow autoplay
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly! User experience first. Autoplay with sound is blocked by policy, muted autoplay or user-initiated play is correct.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Why would browsers block autoplay with sound? Think user experience and data.
blocks.reasoning: Browsers block autoplay with sound to avoid unexpected noise and data usage. Muted autoplay is allowed. Best is controls without autoplay.

blocks.text: Your app is now visual - what's next?

You now know production image patterns: src, alt, width/height for CLS, loading=lazy, figure/figcaption, srcset/sizes for responsive, audio/video with multiple sources and accessibility. Your portfolio now has profile photo, project screenshots with captions, and media - it looks like a real startup site.
